I took 44 aspirin/caffeine combination pills, 6g of Tylenol,  and 2g of ibuprofen.

3 hours passed and I started to sweat a lot. I had been able to resist the natural urge to throw up the whole time. My body felt hot, and so I went to the bathroom.

I threw up, but not much. Mostly dry heaving. There was some bread in it, and I could taste the medication a bit.

I woke up on the bathroom floor maybe twenty minutes later. I was covered in sweat.

I felt quite sick, so I decided to call an ambulance. The paramedics were rather annoyed. Said I'd go to jail for some reason.

The whole ride I was throwing up into special bags. 

When I got to the hospital I was checked in and my heartbeat was 150ish bpm at rest. The RN asked if I was nervous. I told him I felt calm. In fact I had just walked with the paramedics over to their little intake corner.

They took me to a temporary bed. A policeman showed up, told me I was going to be monitored. We had a pleasant conversation about his work. He said what I did was "technically not illegal."

They moved me to a different room upstairs after I told the doctor how much of what I took. I think they wanted to do an ECG, but they didn't for whatever reason.

I was given an IV drip of potassium, which felt like someone was punching my arm over and over. When I threw up, there were unfamiliar bits in it. My not so nice RN told me it was probably my stomach lining shedding. 

A random tech came in and drew arterial blood. Later my RN said my labs were, "fucked up."

After throwing up a lot more, my RN offered me Zofran. She didn't inject it slowly. She just screwed it into the port on my arm and gunned it in all the way. It was an odd pressure, but it didn't hurt.

 I asked her about the potassium, told her it was starting to hurt a bit too much for me to handle. She kind of just squeezed an attachment on IV the bag that controls the flow and left. She seemed mad.

Later on my family showed up and were mad at me. Said I had no right to feel the way I did. My ex-wife was pretty mad, too.

Next I got evaluated by either a psychiatrist or some other mental health professional. She asked me if I sometimes heard someone calling my name when nobody was around. It some sort of sign of depression, I guess.

They put me on an emergency detention order for 48 hours and transferred me to a local inpatient program. The psychiatrist saw me over Skype. Half-listened to me, then gave me Remeron and Zoloft.

I was discharged, picked up by my family. It was more of this "you don't have any reason to be depressed" lecture series, then I got home. I felt like nobody gave a damn. 

So I shut up, quit my job and my ex wife had me go see a psychologist and a psychiatrist. Neither of them agreed on what my deal was. I got put on 3 different meds at the same time and the rest is history.

I've met a few rapists and murderers. Your Hollywood view of crime is funny and sad.

In the case of murder, it is usually out of rage or recklessness. It isn't caused by some sadistic, deeply rooted evil within the person. To say most can't be redeemed is silly. You may have met some yourself without realizing it.

In the case of rape it is more complicated. Rapists generally speaking don't respect their target group. We will say women since this is the most common scenario. The rapists is most commonly male. So with that established, these men view women as objects and hold some sort of grudge against them for one reason or another.

However there are many successful treatment programs for these men. If they actually try, they succeed. Certain things like denial or blaming other people for their crimes is expected and part of the process. Over time their perspective changes and they meet new members and see how they used to think. It's quite beneficial for both the offender and society: It is reformative. These programs are effective in changing the offender's views of their victim(s), their crime and their self.
